naslov: Good Deeds That Do Not Cease Even After Death

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: All praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind.

May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
One of the greatest truths, my respected congregation, is that this world, the dunya, is passing, while the Hereafter, the akhirah, is eternal.
However long a person lives in this world, strives, builds and earns, he must be aware that one day he will leave it and depart from it,

and that his connection with this world will be cut off and his deeds will come to an end, except in a few cases that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, informs us about with the words…
When a person, a human being, passes away, his deeds will come to an end, except in three cases.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: the first case is "sadaqatun jariyah" – ongoing charity: that a person leaves behind him in this world some lasting good, some ongoing charity, such as building a mosque in which people will prostrate to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

We, alhamdulillah, certainly have awareness of this in these lands. We see that when some campaign connected to a mosque or a waqf (endowment) is launched, the money is collected right away, it is built right away, and so on. And that is a great, great blessing. And it is not like that everywhere, dear brothers, it is not like that everywhere. Believe me, it is a great blessing that we have people who are aware of ongoing charity. Also, that a person leaves behind

some hayrat, builds a hayrat (a charitable public drinking fountain) – here too we have awareness, alhamdulillah. When you pass through our villages, you will see fountains by the roadside: a son built one for his father, for his mother, and so on.
A person has to drink, to have some water, to cool down. Also, that a person leaves an orchard from which people will gather fruit and then distribute it to the poor,

and so on, and so forth. For a person who does something like this, some good deed like this, good deeds are written in his book even while he is in the grave, while he is still in the grave. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, further says: "aw 'ilmun yuntafa'u bihi" –

beneficial knowledge: that a person leaves behind beneficial knowledge from which people will benefit. We see how the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, set a limit here, saying: beneficial knowledge, and not that which is not beneficial, that is, knowledge that is useless, that benefits no one. A very important point, dear brothers: that a person teaches himself beneficial knowledge, so that he can pass it on to his children. And there is no better knowledge

than knowledge about Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. So let us not allow someone else to teach our child Al-Fatihah or how to perform the prayer – we should be the first to do that. Why? Because that child, in sha Allah, will tomorrow recite that Fatihah in every rak'ah, will perform the prayer, and all of it is written for us, written there. Or that a person writes some beneficial book and then distributes it, prints it and distributes it; or he does not have to write it – let him take some beneficial book,
on the basics of the faith or something else that benefits people, let him take it, print it and distribute it. Or that a person teaches someone the Qur'an,

or some other science that people will benefit from, in the name of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, for His pleasure, for His pleasure. And the third thing, which is very important, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: that a person leaves behind a good child, a righteous child, who will make dua for him.

A very important point, connected with the upbringing of a child. Believe me, dear brothers, there are people who take their children to matches in Belgrade, in Kraljevo, in Kragujevac, and follow all of it. There is nothing wrong with that, but when it comes to the mekteb (Qur'an school) – he is nowhere to be seen, neither he nor his child.

He will neither see the child off, nor pick him up, nor bring him, nor study with him so that he learns what the efendi assigned. And we see how great a blessing it is, we see how great a blessing it is for a person to raise a child in Islam – a child who will make dua for him,
a child who will make dua for him. What hurts me the most, wallahi, is when I hear someone say: "Efendi, I can't bring my child to the mekteb."
"Why?" He says: "I take him to music lessons." Well, masha Allah! Truly unbelievable. But that is reality. So, taking him to music lessons is more important to you than the mekteb.
Then when you pass away, let him take that violin and play it for you. We do not think, we do not think about how important it is for a person to leave behind a child, a good child.

It is narrated that a man came to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and said to him: "Inna ummiftulitat nafsuha wa azunnuha law takallamat tasaddaqat" – he said: "O Messenger of Allah, my mother passed away suddenly, and I feel that if she had been able to speak, she would have given charity." How important charity is! He further said to the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: "Fa hal laha ajrun in tasaddaqtu 'anha?" –

he said: "Will she have a reward if I give charity on her behalf?" The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Yes, she will have a reward." And that is why, dear brothers, there is no finer reward for our deceased parents than for us to give charity on their behalf.

To give charity on their behalf. And you have people who hold some "fifths," some "sixths," and so on – something that has no basis in the Shari'ah, nor in the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. And what does have a basis – we do not return to that. Go and give charity for your parent, living or dead, and they will have a reward from it.

And those who were disobedient to their parents in this world, and their parents have passed away, and they have returned to the faith – how can you repay your parent? By doing good to him even after his death:

by giving charity for him, by performing umrah for him, by building a hayrat for him. That is how you will best benefit your, your parent. And here, dear brothers, the importance of raising children in Islam is reflected.

How important it is for a person to raise his child well in Islam. Because you are not investing only in the child, you are also investing in yourself, in your rewards, so that both you and your child will benefit on the day when neither money nor anything else will be of use except what a person earned and did in this world.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who worship Him alone. I ask Him, the Exalted, to make us good Muslims, good believers, good neighbours. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive our sins. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin.

بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لِي وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْعَظِيمِ وَنَفَعَنِي وَإِيَّاكُمْ بِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: May Allah bless me and you through the Mighty Qur’an and benefit me and you with the verses and the wise reminder it contains. I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
